utility.notes: The City of Santa Ana's own official resident FAQ, 'How do I set up electricity service?', directs residents to Southern California Edison for electric service setup.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Orange County Power Authority's (OCPA) own official FAQ page explicitly lists its current member cities as Buena Park, Fullerton, and Irvine, with Fountain Valley 'beginning service soon' — Santa Ana is not among them. A secondary source (a chamber-of-commerce blog post) claimed Santa Ana had joined OCPA alongside Irvine/Fullerton/Huntington Beach/Buena Park, but this directly contradicts OCPA's own current, authoritative member list and was not used as evidence per this project's rule against using non-official sources as factual evidence. No other Orange County CCA serving Santa Ana was found, so SCE is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

permit_authority.value: City of Santa Ana Building Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: Directly fetched and confirmed from the city's own official page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Explicitly available to both PG&E and SCE residential customers per the statewide SGIP administrator; SCE administers it within its own distribution territory, which includes Santa Ana/Orange County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for the PG&E-territory records and for Irvine/Fullerton (SCE). Removed the previously-listed "SGIP - Equity Resiliency" line item on 2026-08-09: its expires_on (2025-12-31) has definitively elapsed and no renewal/replacement was confirmed this session, so it no longer represents a current program; the remaining item(s) here are still active/unknown-status per their own status field.

required_documents.notes: Directly confirmed from the city's own page: only the SolarAPP+ Approval Document & Specifications are listed as required for the permit application itself.

value: Contractor must have the SolarAPP+ approval and printed permit available on-site
Inspectors may request additional plans if needed
Inspections are scheduled through the city's separate inspection-scheduling system

value.notes: The city's own page describes SolarAPP+ as providing instant plan review, with revision requests 'processed within 72 business hours,' but does not state an overall submission-to-final-inspection timeline. No specific day range is recorded since none was directly stated for the full permit-to-completion process.

other_conditions: Electrical storage devices (batteries) cannot be visible from public streets and require Planning Division approval for screening
Fire detection and smoke alarms required per Fire Code where applicable
Only licensed, SolarAPP+-registered contractors may apply; permit runners are prohibited
Effective June 1, 2026, all residential solar projects will only be issued permits upon SolarAPP+ approval

eligibility_constraints.notes: The city's own page does not state a maximum system size, so that field is left null rather than assumed.

permit_fees.notes: Not stated in the sources reviewed this session.

rebates.notes: No Santa Ana-specific rebate program was directly confirmed this session, distinct from the statewide SGIP battery incentives already recorded under battery_programs.
